alert: the gateway is intermittently returning 502 Bad Gateway on /orders
note: Rebuilt from stored benchmark results (evals/results/memory-leak-oom.json, session 2026-10-28T00:39:16.000Z, agent run 1). The agent's text, its thinking and the tool outputs were not recorded. This run predates the per-turn trace, so its turns and tool calls are not available. The report, citations and verification are the stored originals.

report.summary: The gateway intermittently returns 502 on /orders because order-service keeps being restarted (restartCount 2, with a restart roughly every 90s). Each restart briefly drops upstream connections, and the storefront sees bursts of 502s. The restarts follow steady memory growth in order-service against its 160 MiB limit.
report.root_cause: Commit dcda15e ("Support Idempotency-Key on order creation") added an in-memory idempotency middleware in order-service. It stores every response in a module-level Map, and also keeps the full raw request body (`request: req.rawBody`) for each key. Nothing is ever evicted and there is no TTL or size cap. Under constant POST /orders traffic, order-service memory grows steadily (78 MiB to 93 MiB within about 15s of uptime) toward its 160 MiB container limit. The process then dies and restarts, and while it is down or restarting the gateway cannot reach it and returns 502. Postgres is healthy and not involved, and the gateway is only the symptom.
